WV-2024-HB5348.s: The law changes the name of the Raleigh County Recreation Authority to the Raleigh County Parks and Recreation Authority. It affects that local board and commission in Raleigh County.

WV-2026-HB4022.s: The law sets how Child Protective Services workers are assigned by county. Their numbers must be based on population, referrals, and average caseload, and cannot go below the bureau’s Jan. 1, 2023 level. The bureau must also send an annual report on any staffing changes and why they were made.

WV-2026-HB4028.s: The law exempts certain materials used to build public school facilities from sales and use tax. It affects construction materials for public school projects in West Virginia.

WV-2026-HB4053.s: The bill would create a blue envelope program in West Virginia. The changed text refers to people diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder, dementia, or intellectual and developmental disabilities.

WV-2026-HB4106.s: This law lets people ages 18 to 20 carry a concealed deadly weapon, which means a hidden weapon, without first getting a license. It also removes a crime tied to carrying a deadly weapon without a license for some people under 21 and changes the rules for minors who may lawfully possess or carry a firearm in certain cases. The law also sets misdemeanor and other criminal penalties for a minor who is convicted of unlawfully carrying a deadly weapon.

WV-2026-HB4138.s: The law expands who must register as a sex offender, including people convicted of certain sex crimes and some other crimes found to be sexually motivated. It also requires more personal details at registration, such as address, employer, vehicles, internet names, phone numbers, and some ID records. People who must register must pay a $125 annual fee, and the money goes to the State Police.

WV-2026-HB4215.s: The law updates state rules for water wells and pump work in West Virginia. It sets certification and permit rules for water well drillers, pump installers, and water well contractors, and it covers how wells may be drilled, changed, or closed. It also sets rules for emergency permits, permit timing, and water well design and safety standards.

WV-2026-HB4354.s: The law sets rules for clothing and other needed items for children who are removed from home and placed in foster, kinship, or residential care. It requires a review at placement, and it sets a minimum initial clothing allowance of $375. It also lays out how the money may be paid, including a reloadable payment card, a purchasing card, or reimbursement to the caregiver.

WV-2026-HB4366.s: This law changes rules for military interpersonal violence cases. It defines some terms, lets a military protective order be used when asking for an emergency protective order or a temporary personal safety order, and requires police to notify the right agencies about possible violations of military protective orders. It applies to people involved in these military and domestic violence cases.

WV-2026-HB4390.s: The law gives some kinship parents a temporary payment equal to a foster parent subsidy when a child is first placed with them, if they pass a background check, the home check, and are assigned help to work toward foster parent certification. The higher payment starts within 30 days of placement and can last for up to six months. It became law in 2026.

WV-2026-HB4412.s: West Virginia passed a law that requires some websites and other online businesses that offer material harmful to minors to check a user’s age before showing that content. It creates civil liability, or the chance to be sued, for publishers and distributors that do not use the required age checks, and it allows the Attorney General to bring cases too. It also sets rules for keeping data, civil penalties, and some exceptions for internet service providers and hosting companies that did not create the material.

WV-2026-HB4433.s: West Virginia’s law on human smuggling and trafficking would update crimes and penalties in those cases. It would add crimes for smuggling adults and minors, change some definitions, and allow civil asset forfeiture in some cases. It would also change rules on restitution, parole, fines, and aggravating circumstances, and create an exemption for medical, mental health, and legal services for an illegal alien. It was approved by the governor and became Chapter 191 in 2026.

WV-2026-HB4463.s: The law changes the powers and duties of the Board of Sanitarians, including setting fees, giving and renewing licenses and certificates, running exams, and handling complaints and discipline. It also sets rules for sanitarian, sanitarian-in-training, and registered sanitarian qualifications, including education, work experience, training hours, and online or in-person training. It lets qualified out-of-state applicants get a West Virginia license or certificate without an exam if they meet certain conditions, and the board must adopt the state’s 2025 universal reciprocity rules by May 1, 2026.

WV-2026-HB4483.s: The law changes rules for funeral service licenses, apprentices, and funeral establishments in West Virginia. It sets or updates license and renewal rules, training and apprenticeship limits, and board powers over inspections, fees, fines, complaints, and continuing education. It also lets a funeral establishment use a provisional licensee in charge for up to 90 days in some cases and creates emeritus licenses for some older license holders.

WV-2026-HB4484.s: County commissions in West Virginia would get broader power to sell or lease county real or personal property. The bill raises the small-item sale cutoff to $10,000, allows some sales by public auction, online auction, competitive bidding, or direct sale to private buyers under set price rules, and lets leases run up to 50 years after a public hearing. It also sets notice and posting rules for some sales and requires some property sold for public use to come back to the county if it is later sold again, unless the deed says otherwise.

WV-2026-HB4538.s: The law changes fines for drivers who break traffic rules in road work zones. It lowers the top fines for failing to obey traffic instructions and for speeding or other traffic rule breaks in construction areas. Drivers who go 15 miles per hour or more over the posted limit in a work zone can also face up to 20 days in jail, or both a fine and jail time.

WV-2026-HB4552.s: The law changes the powers of some Division of Corrections and Rehabilitation officers. It lets certain correctional officers make arrests in set cases, investigate some crimes in correctional facilities, and be approved to carry firearms on duty if they finish required training. It also keeps a special response team and sets rules for concealed carry, firearms training, and related ID cards for qualifying officers.

WV-2026-HB4577.s: The law ties driver’s license and ID card applications to voter registration updates at DMV offices. It also sets rules for sending that voter information to election officials, protecting some of it as private, and says people can opt out of voter registration. It also lets West Virginia recognize driver’s licenses from Ireland and Japan through reciprocal agreements, if those countries meet certain standards.

WV-2026-HB4625.s: The law changes rules for the real estate transfer tax in West Virginia. It says quitclaim deeds are not counted as taxable transfer documents under this chapter. It also changes some tax rules and definitions for people recording deeds and other property transfer papers.

WV-2026-HB4638.s: The law changes voter registration forms to add an option for people to sign up as organ donors and be added to a donor registry. It lets the Secretary of State set up or contract for a system to send donor information to that registry and to share registration records with it. It also requires organ donation information to be included on voter registration cards and says the state will be reimbursed for the costs of building and running the system.

WV-2026-HB4749.s: This law adds three rights for foster children and children in kinship care, which means being raised by relatives or close family friends. It gives children over 13 the right to get timely notice of hearings that may affect them and to attend those hearings. It also says their guardian ad litem, a court-appointed helper, or their lawyer must explain the outcome of any such hearing to them.

WV-2026-HB4755.s: The law adds aggravated vehicular homicide, some DUI offenses, and obstructing emergency responders causing death to the list of crimes that can lead to tougher punishment for repeat offenders. It also creates criminal penalties tied to those offenses. It applies to people convicted of those listed crimes in West Virginia.

WV-2026-HB4765.s: The law changes pay rules for West Virginia State Police members and certain forensic lab staff. It sets new base pay starting July 1, 2026, with pay ranging from $52,644 for cadets in training to $90,102 for forensic scientist supervisor IV, and it adds service-step raises and up to $200 in extra pay per pay period for some state police members. It also starts a new market pay add-on based on local income data on December 1, 2026, with payments beginning July 1, 2027, and limited to 20% of base pay.

WV-2026-HB4798.s: The law lets schools use wearable panic alert devices, or mobile alert buttons, in public schools if funding is available. These devices must connect with 911 and help trigger a schoolwide lockdown notice, and school staff who use them must be trained each year. It also creates a state fund for this equipment and related school safety gear, and the law ends on December 31, 2029.

WV-2026-HB4819.s: The law changes how criminal records can be used when deciding whether someone may get a license or other approval to work in a profession. If a criminal background check is used, it must include the outcome of any arrest or charge. It applies to people seeking approval to practice certain jobs in West Virginia, and it became law in 2026.

WV-2026-HB4842.s: The law lets a person who is identifiable in a private intimate image sue if someone intentionally shares or threatens to share it without consent and knew or acted with reckless disregard about that lack of consent, privacy, and identity. It also says that agreeing to take the image or sharing it before does not by itself mean the person agreed to later disclosure. People found liable under the law can be held together for the full damage award. It became law in 2026.

WV-2026-HB4865.s: The law lets local election leaders create a program for high school juniors and seniors, including home-schooled students, to train and serve as election officials. These students must meet set voting, age, school, approval, and training rules, and only one such trainee may serve per party in each precinct. The law also lets county leaders suspend an election official’s ability to serve for certain problems, such as not showing up, bad conduct, or interfering with voters.

WV-2026-HB4951.s: Requires doctors with MD and DO licenses to complete continuing medical education to renew their licenses. It also adds nutrition training rules for people licensed on or before July 1, 2026, and for new license holders after that date, with timing based on the next renewal or within one year of initial licensure. The measure became law in 2026.

WV-2026-HB4983.s: The law lets the Department of Commerce use a state rule on certifying a microgrid district or a high impact data center. It also approves a related rule for tourism development districts, and adds language about the use or access of water in one part of the data center rule.

WV-2026-HB4990.s: The bill creates crimes for stealing, tampering with, or tricking someone to get gift cards or gift card access info. It sets different penalties based on value, with misdemeanor charges under $1,000 and felony charges over $1,000. The law applies to people who act with intent to defraud and became Chapter 105 in 2026.

WV-2026-HB4996.s: This law changes rules for false emergency reports and threats of violent crime. It makes some threats to commit violence a felony and lets courts bar certain people on release from living or working within 1,000 feet of the threatened place or person. It also lets courts order repayment of emergency response costs, and it does not apply to an authorized emergency drill.

WV-2026-HB5048.s: The law requires foster children who are waiting for a new placement to keep getting school through virtual learning. It sets rules for which county provides that learning, gives state education tech training to the person or group caring for the child, and says virtual classes should start within three days. When the child is placed with a foster family, school and login info must be sent to the family and the new county.

WV-2026-HB5065.s: The law changes how hotel occupancy taxes are collected in cities and counties. It says the guest pays the tax, and hotels and online booking services must collect and send it to the right local tax office. It also sets rules for online booking services that handle enough West Virginia sales or transactions, including record keeping and how to send the money.

WV-2026-HB5110.s: The law changes West Virginia rules for tuition and fee waivers or adjustments at public colleges for older adults who audit classes, which means take the class without credit. It lowers the age limit from 65 to 60 and says that, for the no-credit option, any extra tuition for eligible nonresident students cannot be more than 50% of the rate for West Virginia residents.

WV-2026-HB5214.s: The law lets a court require drug testing before a child is returned home to parents who were found to have abused or neglected the child, especially when drug use may have led to the child’s removal or there is reason to think drug use may still be happening. If a test is positive, the court, guardian ad litem, and other parties must be told, and the lab must confirm the result. The Department of Human Services must pay the reasonable and needed cost of this testing.

WV-2026-HB5288.s: This bill would add $200,000 in special revenue to the West Virginia Spay Neuter Assistance Fund in the Department of Agriculture for fiscal year 2026. The money would be for current expenses in that program. It was approved by the governor and became law.

WV-2026-HB5307.s: The bill adds $10 million from the state’s general revenue surplus for the Department of Tourism’s Division of Culture and History. The money is for capital outlay, repairs, and equipment in fiscal year 2026. It became law in 2026.

WV-2026-HB5353.s: The bill would treat virtual currency kiosks, like machines that exchange cash for virtual currency, as money transmitters that need a state license. It would also require them to give disclosures and set daily limits on transactions for new and existing customers. The bill was approved by the governor and became law in 2026.

WV-2026-HB5364.s: The measure became law in 2026. It would change how some state boards and commissions are handled. It also directs royalties from leasing state-owned gas, oil, and other mineral rights under the Ohio River and its tributaries into the West Virginia Parks and Recreation Endowment Fund.

WV-2026-HB5366.s: The law sets rules for the practice of law in West Virginia, including lawyer ethics, judicial ethics, and discipline for attorneys. It keeps the West Virginia State Bar as part of the court system and requires lawyers in the state to be members in good standing. It also lets the court set fees for running the system, with yearly fees capped at $5 unless most lawyers agree to pay more, and makes certain assistance program records confidential if the court says so.

WV-2026-HB5437.s: The law sets up a new license for vape or smoke shops in West Virginia and requires them to follow state rules to operate. It sets application and background check rules for owners and managers, and it limits who can get or keep a license based on certain criminal history and other qualifications. Running a shop without the license can lead to a misdemeanor charge, with a fine of up to $10,000 and jail time of up to one year.

WV-2026-HB5480.s: The law sets up a West Virginia youth summer job and career readiness program. It lets the state work with local agencies, give grant money to employer partners, and use a special fund, grants, and donations to support the program. It also requires yearly reports and sets rules for how the program runs.

WV-2026-HB5484.s: This law creates new felony crimes tied to blocking or forcing medical care. It covers a person’s right to get medical treatment or medical forensic care after a sexual offense, and it also includes forcing or pressuring someone into an illegal abortion. It applies to people involved in these acts and sets criminal penalties.

WV-2026-HB5515.s: The law updates West Virginia workers’ compensation rules for reporting injuries and paying claims. It requires workers and employers to report injuries faster, and it sets steps for paying temporary disability and medical benefits while a claim is being reviewed. It also says benefits are paid directly to the claimant and gives rules for when overpaid amounts can be recovered.

WV-2026-HB5527.s: The law sets rules for wellness reimbursement programs, which are extra health or wellness benefits tied to insurance or self-insured health plans. It requires program administrators to get a state license, pay fees, keep records, and follow federal and state rules. It also gives the Insurance Commissioner power to inspect records, fine or revoke licenses, and enforce the law, and it sets penalties for violations.

WV-2026-HB5528.s: This law lets certain public officials and some family members ask a government agency to remove or hide their home address, personal phone numbers, and related name details from public online records. If the agency does not do that after a written request, the person may go to court, and the agency may have to pay court costs and lawyer fees. The law still allows some sharing of this information for government work, law enforcement, legal process, property records, election work, and certain other listed uses.

WV-2026-HB5582.s: The law extends a drug screening program for adults who apply for Temporary Assistance for Needy Families cash aid in West Virginia, through December 31, 2026, if federal approval is given. If a case worker finds reasonable suspicion, the person must take a drug test, and the human services department pays for the first test and the screening program. People who test positive may have to enter treatment and job skills programs, while children in the home keep their benefits and may have a protective payee named to receive them.

WV-2026-HB5612.s: The law changes how the state reports and tracks real property it owns or leases. It requires each agency to mark properties that are unused or mostly unused, and it removes the rule that the state must set a market value for that property. It affects state agencies and property on the State Capitol Complex.

WV-2026-HB5638.s: This law changes the state cybersecurity program and expands the duties of the state chief information security officer. It creates a West Virginia Cybersecurity Office, sets rules and standards for state agencies, and requires agencies to do cyber risk reviews and follow security policies. It also lets the office charge some exempt public bodies for voluntary help and protects certain cybersecurity records from public release.

WV-2026-HB5682.s: The law moves $35 million from the Governor’s Office Civil Contingent Fund into the state’s general revenue surplus. It then gives that money to the Higher Education Policy Commission for administration. It applies to the fiscal year ending June 30, 2026.

WV-2026-HB5684.s: The law lets the state Supreme Court create child protection commissioners to handle child protection cases. It sets rules for who can serve, how they are appointed and supervised, what they can do, and how they are paid. It also gives some retirement benefit rules for certain retired public workers who take these jobs and lets senior judges and justices serve as commissioners.

WV-2026-HB5689.s: The bill would add state money from a surplus fund to the Department of Homeland Security for fiscal year 2026. It would increase funding for Information Technology Services by $6,642,874 and Special Services by $5,002,392 for correctional units.

WV-2026-HB5690.s: The bill adds $4,025,000 in state general revenue for the Adjutant General for fiscal year 2026. The money is for an Armory Board transfer from surplus funds. It affects the Adjutant General's office and its spending for that year.

WV-2026-HB5692.s: The bill adds $100 million from the State Road Fund to the West Virginia Division of Highways for other federal aid programs in fiscal year 2026. It would increase money for the Department of Transportation for the year ending June 30, 2026. The bill became law.
